title: Connectedness, separations, and connected components
terms: connected space; disconnected space; separation; connected component.

exposition.text:
A separation is a representation of a space as two disjoint nonempty relatively open subsets. A
space is connected if no separation exists; equivalently its only clopen subsets are ∅ and the
whole space. Connected subsets of R are exactly intervals, with singletons and the empty set
included.
Unions of connected sets with a common point are connected. If A is connected and A ⊆ B ⊆
A, then B is connected; products of connected spaces are connected. A connected component
is a maximal connected subset. Use a continuous map to a discrete set, or a visible clopen
partition, to disprove connectedness.

question.text:
How many connected components does R \ ({0} ∪ {1/n : n ≥ 1}) have?
(A) 1
(B) 2
(C) 3
(D) Countably infinitely many.
(E) Uncountably many.

solution.text:
The components are (−∞, 0), (1, ∞), and the intervals (1/(n + 1), 1/n) for n ≥ 1. Each is an
interval, and no connected subset can cross a removed point.

question.text:
Let A = {(x, sin(1/x)) : 0 < x ≤ 1} and B = A ∪ ({0} × [−1, 1]). Which conclusion follows from
connectedness and closure alone?
(A) B is disconnected.
(B) B is connected.
2
(C) B is open in R .
(D) A is compact.
(E) B has exactly two connected components.

solution.text:
A is the continuous image of the interval (0, 1], hence is connected. Its closure is B, and
the closure of a connected set is connected. This argument asserts connectedness without
asserting path connectedness.

question.text:
How many connected components does R \ Q have?
(A) One
(B) Uncountably many
(C) Countably infinitely many
(D) Zero
(E) Two

solution.text:
Every connected subset of R is an interval. Any interval containing two distinct points
contains a rational, so a connected subset of the irrationals has at most one point. Thus all
components are singletons.

question.text:
A continuous map from a nonempty connected space to the discrete set {0, 1, 2} must have
image of size
(A) Any of 1, 2, 3 (B) 0 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) 1

solution.text:
Continuous images of connected spaces are connected. The only nonempty connected
subsets of a discrete space are singletons, so such a map is constant.

question.text:
If connected subsets A, B have nonempty intersection, which must be connected?
(A) The complement of A ∪ B (B) A \ B (C) ∂A (D) A ∪ B (E) A ∩ B

solution.text:
A separation of the union would place each connected subset wholly on one side. Their
common point forces the same side for both, contradicting a nontrivial separation.

How many connected components does (R \ {0}) have in the product topology?
(A) 2 (B) 3 (C) 6 (D) 8 (E) Infinitely many

solution.text:
Each coordinate has two connected components, the negative and positive rays. The eight
sign choices produce products of three intervals, each connected. A connected subset
cannot meet two different sign choices, since a coordinate projection would then be a con-
nected subset of R \ {0} containing both signs. Thus these eight products are exactly the
components.
